meta.gift: memory, tide, and the salt that keeps names from dissolving
meta.waning: the tide recedes from the world's edges; memories thin and the drowned begin to speak
meta.curse_desc: salt blooms beneath the skin; the afflicted forget faces first, then their own
veils: The church drowns its saints not to honour the Radiance but to silence what they heard in the tide.
The Radiance never drowned — it was drowned, by the very gods who now pray for its return.
The gods drowned it in mercy, at its own asking: it had begun to remember the world before this one, and memory is contagious.
meta.epigraph: Of the Drowned Radiance little now is spoken, and less is true. Gather what the old things still remember, and be sparing with belief.

ages.name: the Age of the Gift
ages.blurb: the Drowned Radiance gave the world memory, tide, and the salt that keeps names from dissolving.

ages.name: the Age of Names
ages.blurb: The gods withdrew to their high seats and mortals learned to matter. Then the waning began: the tide recedes from the world's edges; memories thin and the drowned begin to speak.

ages.name: the Age of Dusk
ages.blurb: The present age. The gods are silent, the roads belong to the marked, and pilgrims walk toward rumours of a cure.

e1.text: the Drowned Radiance rose (or was raised — the tellings differ) and gave the world memory, tide, and the salt that keeps names from dissolving.

e2.text: Veloryne, god of storms and unkept promises, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e3.text: Nimos, god of harvest, plenty, and the debt of plenty, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e4.text: Sylorien, god of law, chains, and the first covenant, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e5.text: Nyadra, god of secrets, locks, and the spaces between, claimed a portion of the gift and took a throne.

e7.text: The Brine of Veloryne was wrought as regalia of Veloryne's throne.

e9.text: The Pearl of Nimos was wrought as regalia of Nimos's throne.

e11.text: The Salt of Sylorien was wrought as regalia of Sylorien's throne.

e13.text: The Brine of Nyadra was wrought as regalia of Nyadra's throne.

e14.text: Ishirula, the Still Water, rose against the thrones. Nimos led the gods to war.
e14.hidden: Veloryne treated with Ishirula in secret and was spared what followed.

e15.text: Ishirula was defeated and sealed beneath Aldranarahollow; the seal was bought with the lives of 9 champions.

e16.text: The waning began: the tide recedes from the world's edges; memories thin and the drowned begin to speak. Mortals called the affliction the Brine-hollowing: salt blooms beneath the skin; the afflicted forget faces first, then their own.

e17.text: Aldrulmere the Lantern-eyed founded the Order of the Brine at Olulthasshroud, sworn to stand against the Brine-hollowing.

e18.text: The Church of Veloryne was raised at Ostenthasvault; Thalenien the Unbowed took its first pulpit, preaching that the waning is a trial and the faithful will be spared.

e19.text: Maziadra the Lantern-eyed was cast out of Church of Veloryne and founded the Cult of the Second Dawn, teaching that the gods themselves caused the waning.
e19.hidden: The heresy is nearer the truth than the sermon.

e20.text: Ezric the Forsworn united the river-clans and was crowned in Quelwynbarrow; the realm took the name Hestnothgate.

e21.text: At the urging of Thalenien, the saint Yormere the Adamant was given to the Drowned Radiance in the rite of restoration. For a generation, the waning slowed.
e21.hidden: The rite did not restore anything. It only fed the waning more slowly — and Thalenien suspected as much.

e22.text: Hestirdane the Grey, sword-hand of Ezric, opened the gates of Quelwynbarrow to the Order of the Brine over a grievance no chronicle agrees on.
e22.hidden: Hestirdane acted on a promise from the Cult of the Second Dawn: that the marked of their house would be spared the Brine-hollowing. The promise was not kept.

e23.text: Hestnothgate fell. Ezric the Forsworn died at the foot of their own throne; the crown was carried away and never worn again.

e24.text: Hestirdane was found at Olulthasshroud bearing the Brine-hollowing, and was not spared.

e25.text: Sylorien, god of law, chains, and the first covenant, descended below the world to look upon the Drowned Radiance directly, and did not return.
e25.hidden: Sylorien found the truth of the waning, and chose to stay.

e26.text: Mazamund the Unmarked, last-sworn of the Order of the Brine, set out for the place where Sylorien was lost, carrying the order's final blessing.

e27.text: Mazamund returned once, said nothing, left their sword upon the order's altar, and walked into the dusk unarmed.

e28.text: Pilgrims of the Cult of the Second Dawn were found digging at the seal of Ishirula. The wardens hanged nine; the digging continued.
e28.hidden: The seal has been failing on its own since the waning began. The cult only follows the cracks.

e29.text: The saint was not the first choice. The first choice ran, and was let run; the chronicles kept the saint's serenity and lost the running.
e29.hidden: The one who ran was never pursued, by design.

e30.text: The procession took the long road, through every village, so that all might see what their deliverance cost. Veremis walked at the saint's left hand and never afterward spoke of it.

e31.text: The war's worst day was at Seriaachvault, where the line held for a night and a morning under Solemis of the Rearguard, and then did not hold.

e32.text: Before the last assault, champions met between the hosts, as the old law required. What was said there was not recorded; what was done there decided the war.
e32.hidden: The duel was not fought to a death but to a bargain.
